name: Nikolaus von Schönberg
summary:
Nikolaus von Schönberg was a German Catholic cardinal and Archbishop of Capua from 1503 until his death in 1537. He played a key role in the Council of Trent, where he contributed to the reform of the Catholic Church. As Archbishop, von Schönberg oversaw numerous architectural projects in Capua, including the construction of the Cathedral of San Severino.

Von Schönberg's legacy extends beyond his ecclesiastical duties, as he was a patron of the arts and supported various scholars and artists during his lifetime. His contributions to the Catholic Church have had a lasting impact on Christian theology and practice.

The city of Capua continues to celebrate its connection to von Schönberg through various cultural events and historical reenactments. This enduring legacy serves as a testament to the significant influence he had on the region during his lifetime.

In a remarkable display of his dedication, von Schönberg worked tirelessly until his death at the age of 65, leaving behind a lasting impact on the Catholic Church and the city of Capua.
